samasa.explanation: aṣṭan 'eight' qualifies mūrti 'form, embodiment', and the whole points outside itself to the Goddess: 'She who has eight forms'. The numeral's final n is dropped at the end of a compound member (aṣṭan → aṣṭa-), a morphological change, not sandhi; mūrti keeps its i-stem and the nominative is aṣṭamūrtiḥ.

components.note: appears as aṣṭa- in the compound

names.meaning: She who has eight forms
names.significance: Traditionally the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti) of Śiva — earth, water, fire, air, space, sun, moon and the sacrificer — which She, as His power, also is. The eightfold nature (prakṛti) of Bhagavad Gītā 7.4 is another octad read here.

samasa.explanation: jaitrī 'victorious, conqueror' is the head; ajā 'the unborn (she)' stands to it as the one conquered: 'the conqueror of Ajā'. Ajā is the feminine of aja 'unborn' and, after Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.5 (ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇām, 'the one unborn [she] of red, white and black'), names beginningless Māyā or ignorance. The two members meet with no sound change.

components.meaning: the unborn one (feminine); Māyā, beginningless ignorance

components.note: feminine of jaitra 'victorious', a vṛddhi derivative of jetṛ 'conqueror' (√ji 'to conquer')

names.meaning: She who conquers Ajā, the unborn Māyā of ignorance
names.significance: Traditionally Ajā is avidyā, without beginning but not without end: She who is Knowledge overcomes it in the devotee.

meaning_check.note: 'ignorance' is the traditional sense of Ajā, not the word itself; the meaning now names Ajā and gives the sense.

names.previous_split_issues: ajā was glossed 'not' (as if a- 'not' + jā); it is ajā 'the unborn (she)'. The second member was given as jetrī; the text reads jaitrī (vṛddhi ai).
names.variants: The site's earlier text read अजाजेत्री (ajājetrī, feminine of jetṛ 'conqueror'), with the same sense; the verse reads jaitrī (see the correction log).

samasa.vigraha: लोकस्य यात्रा लोकयात्रा; लोकयात्राम् विदधाति इति लोकयात्राविधायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: lokasya yātrā lokayātrā; lokayātrām vidadhāti iti lokayātrāvidhāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) loka-yātrā 'the course, the going-on of the world' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, yātrā the head). (2) vidhāyinī 'one who arranges, ordains' is an agent noun in -in from vi + √dhā, with the y inserted after a root in ā; it governs lokayātrā as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa): 'She who ordains the course of the world'.

components.meaning: world; the people of the world
going on, course, the conduct of life

names.meaning: She who directs the course of the worlds
names.significance: Traditionally the ongoing life of the worlds — creation, sustenance and the working-out of each being's karma — runs by Her ordinance.
names.previous_split_issues: yātrā was given with a short final a (yātra); the word is yātrā, as the corrected text reads.

components.note: eka 'one' + the suffix -ākin 'alone' (Pāṇini 5.3.52 ekād ākinic cāsahāye), feminine -ī; eka's final a is dropped before the suffix

names.meaning: She who is the lone One
names.significance: Before creation there is nothing beside Her; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (1.4.3) says the Self, being alone (ekākī), did not delight and wished for a second. She is the One without a second (ekam evādvitīyam, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2.1).

meaning_check.note: Capitalized 'One' to mark the metaphysical sense; wording otherwise kept.

samasa.explanation: rūpa 'form, nature' is qualified by bhūman 'plenitude' in apposition, and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is the Plenitude'. bhūman is an n-stem; its n is dropped at the end of a compound member (bhūma-), a morphological change, not sandhi.

components.note: abstract noun from bahu 'much' (bahu becomes bhū, Pāṇini 6.4.158 bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ); bhūma- in the compound

components.meaning: having the form, of the nature
components.note: rūpa 'form' with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose form is the Bhūman, the boundless Plenitude
names.significance: The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.23–24) teaches that 'the Plenitude (bhūmā) alone is happiness': where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else, that is the Bhūman. Taking bhūman as 'manyness', the name also means that She is the sum of all that exists.

meaning_check.note: 'the aggregate of all existing things' takes bhūman only as 'multitude'; the name's classic source is the Upaniṣadic Bhūman, the Infinite. The aggregate reading is kept in the significance.

names.previous_split_issues: bhūma was given without its stem (bhūman) and glossed adjectivally ('infinite/all-pervading'); it is the noun bhūman 'plenitude'.
names.uncertain: bhūman can mean 'the Infinite' (Chāndogya 7.23–24) or 'manyness, the aggregate'; both are current for this name.

sandhi.rule: the final s of nis becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

samasa.explanation: nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone away', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom duality has gone', i.e. in whom there is no duality. dvaita takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi.

components.note: prefix; nir- before a voiced sound
dvaita, from dvi 'two' (dvīta 'twofold' with vṛddhi), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is without duality
names.significance: Traditionally: nothing exists beside Her to make a second, so duality has no place in Her nature.

meaning_check.note: 'the sense of' is not in the name; the name denies duality itself, not only the perception of it.

names.previous_split_issues: nir was given in its sandhi form; the prefix is nis (r only before a voiced sound).

samasa.explanation: The participle varjitā 'devoid, left out' is the head; dvaita 'duality' stands to it in the instrumental: 'devoid of duality'. The members meet with no sound change.

components.meaning: devoid of, free from, excluded from
components.note: causative of √vṛj 'to turn away', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is beyond duality
names.significance: With name 667 it states non-duality twice: no second exists in Her, and She remains untouched by the dualities of the world She manifests.

samasa.explanation: -da 'giving' from √dā (suffix ka after a root in ā preceded by its object, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), feminine -dā; anna is its object: 'giver of food'.

names.meaning: She who is the giver of food to all living things
names.significance: Traditionally She is Annapūrṇā, the nourisher of all; the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (3.2) teaches 'food is Brahman', the first step of Bhṛgu's inquiry.

samasa.explanation: As in name 669: -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and vasu 'wealth' its object.

names.meaning: She who is the giver of wealth
names.significance: Traditionally wealth of every kind — material prosperity and the inner riches of virtue and knowledge — flows from Her.

names.meaning: She who is ancient
names.significance: She is older than all that exists, the first before creation; the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (4.3) addresses the One as the old man who totters with a staff, as well as the youth and the maiden.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
vṛddhi: a + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्म च आत्मा च ब्रह्मात्मानौ; ब्रह्मात्मनोः ऐक्यम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम्; ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम् एव स्वरूपम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: brahma ca ātmā ca brahmātmānau; brahmātmanoḥ aikyam brahmātmaikyam; brahmātmaikyam eva svarūpam brahmātmaikyasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) brahman and ātman, the absolute and the Self, are joined as a dvandva (both stems lose their final n, a morphological change). (2) aikya 'oneness' takes them in the genitive: 'the oneness of Brahman and the Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with svarūpa 'own nature' (karmadhāraya). (4) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) makes 'she who has this as her own nature'.

components.note: appears as brahma- in the compound
appears as ātma- in the compound
abstract noun from eka 'one', with vṛddhi
sva 'own' + rūpa 'form, nature' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

names.meaning: She whose very nature is the oneness of Brahman and the Self (Ātman)
names.significance: The central teaching of the Upaniṣads (tat tvam asi, ahaṃ brahmāsmi): the Self and Brahman are not two. She is that identity itself, not a union of two things.

meaning_check.note: aikya is 'oneness, identity', not 'union', which implies two things joined; Brahman and Ātman capitalized in IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: brahmātmaikya was left as one row; it is brahman + ātman + aikya, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha and vṛddhi.

components.note: feminine of bṛhat, present participle of √bṛh 'to grow, expand'

names.meaning: She who is immense
names.significance: She is Brahman, the word itself coming from the same root √bṛh 'to grow great'. Bṛhatī is also the name of a Vedic metre.

components.meaning: belonging to Brahman; a woman of the priestly class
components.note: feminine of brāhmaṇa, a derivative of brahman

names.meaning: She who is Brāhmaṇī, belonging to Brahman
names.significance: Traditionally the brāhmaṇa is the type of sattva, the quality of clarity and calm, and so the name is read as 'She in whom sattva predominates'. Brāhmaṇī is also a name of the Śakti of Brahmā.

meaning_check.note: 'predominantly sāttvic' is an interpretation, not what the word says; it is kept in the significance and the meaning now gives the word.

names.uncertain: Several readings are current: 'of the nature of Brahman', 'predominantly sāttvic' (the brāhmaṇa as sattva), and the Śakti of Brahmā; the source of the sāttvic gloss could not be confirmed.

components.meaning: belonging to Brahmā or Brahman; speech, Sarasvatī
components.note: feminine of brāhma, a vṛddhi derivative of brahman

names.meaning: She who is Brāhmī, the power of speech
names.significance: Brāhmī is a classical name of speech and of Sarasvatī; She is also the Śakti of Brahmā, first of the Mothers (Mātṛkās).

meaning_check.note: The name is Brāhmī, speech itself; 'presides over' was added. The sense is kept.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्मणः आनन्दः ब्रह्मानन्दः; ब्रह्मानन्दः यस्याः सा ब्रह्मानन्दा
samasa.vigraha_iast: brahmaṇaḥ ānandaḥ brahmānandaḥ; brahmānandaḥ yasyāḥ sā brahmānandā
samasa.explanation: (1) brahma-ānanda 'the bliss of Brahman' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; brahman loses its n). (2) As a bahuvrīhi with the feminine -ā: 'She whose (very being) is the bliss of Brahman'. A karmadhāraya reading, 'She who is the bliss that is Brahman', gives the same sense.

components.note: appears as brahma- in the compound
ānanda, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose being is the bliss of Brahman
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2.4, 2.9) speaks of 'the bliss of Brahman' (ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān), knowing which one fears nothing; She is that bliss.

meaning_check.note: 'ever immersed in' is not in the name; She is the bliss, not one immersed in it.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; brahmānandā is brahman + ānanda, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.explanation: priya 'dear' and bali 'offering' are joined as a bahuvrīhi with priya placed second (as in guḍapriya 'fond of molasses'): 'She to whom offerings are dear'. If bali is taken from balin 'the strong' (n dropped in the compound), the vigraha is balinaḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā, 'She to whom the strong are dear'.

components.note: priya, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is fond of offerings (bali)
names.significance: Traditionally the true offering is the self — the devotee's ego offered into Her; worship (pūjā) closes with bali to Her attendant powers.

meaning_check.note: 'especially' and 'sacrificial' were added; the name says 'to whom offerings are dear'.

names.uncertain: bali may also be read from balin 'the strong': 'She who loves the strong' (those strong in devotion and self-mastery).

samasa.explanation: rūpa 'form' is identified with bhāṣā 'speech, language', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is language'.

components.note: rūpa 'form' with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is in the form of language
names.significance: Every language, sacred or common, is a form of Her as Vāk (speech); all words are Her body, as the alphabet (mātṛkā) is in Śrīvidyā.

samasa.explanation: bṛhat 'vast' qualifies senā 'army', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose army is vast'. The feminine bṛhatī takes its masculine stem bṛhat before another member of a bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva). t and s meet with no change.

names.meaning: She who has a vast army
names.significance: In the Lalitopākhyāna Her hosts of śaktis, led by Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā, march against Bhaṇḍāsura; inwardly they are Her countless powers.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: न भावः अभावः; भावः च अभावः च भावाभावौ; भावाभावाभ्याम् विवर्जिता भावाभावविवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: na bhāvaḥ abhāvaḥ; bhāvaḥ ca abhāvaḥ ca bhāvābhāvau; bhāvābhāvābhyām vivarjitā bhāvābhāvavivarjitā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-bhāva 'non-being' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) bhāva-abhāva 'being and non-being' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) The participle vivarjitā 'wholly devoid' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: 'devoid of being and non-being'.

components.note: vi + causative of √vṛj 'to turn away', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is beyond being and non-being
names.significance: She cannot be called existent or non-existent in the ordinary sense: 'then there was neither non-being nor being' (Ṛgveda 10.129.1); 'it is called neither being nor non-being' (Bhagavad Gītā 13.12).
names.previous_split_issues: bhāvābhāva was left as one row; it is bhāva + abhāva, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; sukha 'ease' stands to it in the instrumental of manner: 'to be worshipped with ease'. A reading with sukha as 'joy' — 'to be worshipped joyfully' — is also possible.

names.meaning: She who is easily worshipped
names.significance: Traditionally Her worship needs no harsh austerity: devotion, Her name and simple offerings please Her, and the worship is itself a joy.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; sukhārādhyā is sukha + ārādhyā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.explanation: -kara 'making, doing' from √kṛ (suffix ṭa, which takes the feminine -ī: karī) is the head; śubha 'good, auspicious' is its object: 'maker of the auspicious'.

names.meaning: She who brings about what is auspicious
names.significance: She works good for Her devotees — prosperity here and liberation hereafter.

meaning_check.note: 'does good' made more exact: śubha is the auspicious, the good that She brings about.

names.meaning: She who is the auspicious goal, easily reached
names.significance: Bhāskararāya counts the three words śobhanā sulabhā gatiḥ as one name, since śobhanā alone would repeat name 462. She is the goal (gati) of all, and for those who love Her that goal is near.

meaning_check.note: gati is primarily 'goal, refuge' (the destination), and the name calls Her that goal; 'attained through a … path' made Her the one reached by a path.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; the name is three separate words (śobhanā, sulabhā, gatiḥ).
names.uncertain: Not a compound: the adjectives keep their feminine -ā, which they would lose inside a karmadhāraya (śobhana-sulabha-gati); the name is three nominatives in apposition, counted as one name. gati can be 'goal' or 'path'.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: राज्ञाम् राजा राजराजः; राजराजानाम् ईश्वरी राजराजेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: rājñām rājā rājarājaḥ; rājarājānām īśvarī rājarājeśvarī
samasa.explanation: (1) rāja-rāja 'king of kings' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa); rājan as the last member of a tatpuruṣa ends in -a (samāsānta ṭac, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac), and as first member loses its n. (2) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head: 'sovereign of the kings of kings'. Rājarāja is also a title of Kubera, giving 'the sovereign of Kubera'.

components.note: rājan as last member of rājarāja, with the compound-final -a

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the kings of kings
names.significance: Rājarājeśvarī is one of the principal names of the Śrīvidyā Goddess: She rules over every ruler, the guardians of the world and the lord of wealth alike.

meaning_check.note: 'kings and emperors' smoothed out the compound; it is 'the kings of kings', with rājarāja also Kubera.

names.previous_split_issues: rājeśvarī was glossed 'queen of queens'; it is rāja (from rājarāja 'king of kings') + īśvarī 'sovereign', joined by guṇa.
names.uncertain: rājarāja may be 'kings of kings' (emperors) or Kubera, the king of the yakṣas; both readings are current.

samasa.explanation: dāyinī 'giving' is an agent noun in -in from √dā (with y inserted after a root in ā), feminine; it governs rājya 'kingdom, dominion' as its object.

names.meaning: She who gives dominion
names.significance: She grants outward rule, and inwardly the sovereignty of the Self (svārājya), mastery over one's own mind and senses.

samasa.explanation: vallabha 'dear, beloved' and rājya 'kingdom, sovereignty' are joined as a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom sovereignty is dear'. Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (rājyasya vallabhā) it means 'the beloved of the kingdom'.

names.meaning: She to whom sovereignty is dear
names.significance: With names 684–685 it shows Her as the sovereign who delights in rule, cherishes the realm, and gives dominion to Her devotees.

meaning_check.note: vallabha means 'dear, beloved', not 'protecting'; the name says the realm is dear to Her (or She is its beloved).

names.uncertain: vallabha also means 'lord, overseer' in some lexicons, which would support 'protector of kingdoms'; the bahuvrīhi 'to whom sovereignty is dear' and the tatpuruṣa 'beloved of the realm' are the plain readings.

samasa.explanation: The participle rājat 'shining' qualifies kṛpā 'compassion', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose compassion shines'. The feminine rājantī takes its masculine stem rājat inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); t and k meet with no change.

names.meaning: She whose compassion shines forth
names.significance: Her grace is not hidden: it shines, like a ruler's splendor, on all who turn to Her. The participle also echoes rājan 'king', continuing the royal names around it.

meaning_check.note: rājat is 'shining, resplendent', not 'captivating'.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; rājatkṛpā is rājat 'shining' + kṛpā 'compassion'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: राज्ञः पीठम् राजपीठम्; राजपीठे निवेशिताः राजपीठनिवेशिताः; निजाः आश्रिताः निजाश्रिताः; राजपीठनिवेशिताः निजाश्रिताः यया सा राजपीठनिवेशितनिजाश्रिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: rājñaḥ pīṭham rājapīṭham; rājapīṭhe niveśitāḥ rājapīṭhaniveśitāḥ; nijāḥ āśritāḥ nijāśritāḥ; rājapīṭhaniveśitāḥ nijāśritāḥ yayā sā rājapīṭhaniveśitanijāśritā
samasa.explanation: (1) rāja-pīṭha 'royal seat, throne' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan loses its n). (2) rājapīṭha-niveśita 'placed on the throne' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the causative participle). (3) nija-āśrita 'Her own dependents, those who take refuge in Her' (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental yayā: 'She by whom Her own dependents are seated on royal thrones'. The participle stands first, as is usual in a bahuvrīhi.

components.note: appears as rāja- in the compound
ni + causative of √viś 'to enter, settle', past participle
ā + √śri 'to resort to', past participle; feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who seats on royal thrones those who take refuge in Her
names.significance: She raises Her devotees to sovereignty — worldly, and inwardly to the throne of the Self.

meaning_check.note: Grammar of the old sentence repaired; the sense is unchanged.

names.previous_split_issues: nijāśritā was glossed 'her own devotees' as one row; it is nija 'own' + āśritā 'one who has taken refuge', joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.explanation: lakṣmī 'fortune, prosperity, the goddess Lakṣmī' is the head and rājya 'kingdom' stands to it in the genitive: 'the fortune of the kingdom'. lakṣmī keeps the nominative -ḥ (it is not a derived feminine in -ī; compare name 210).

components.meaning: fortune, prosperity, royal splendor; the goddess Lakṣmī

names.meaning: She who is the Fortune (Lakṣmī) of the kingdom
names.significance: Rājyalakṣmī is the goddess of a realm's prosperity and royal splendor; where She dwells, the kingdom flourishes.

meaning_check.note: rājya is 'kingdom, sovereignty', not 'the world'.

samasa.explanation: nāthā 'mistress, protector' is the head; kośa 'treasury' (or 'sheath') stands to it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the mistress of the treasury
names.significance: As queen She owns the treasury of the realm. Kośa also means 'sheath', so the name is read inwardly as 'Lord of the five sheaths (kośas)' that cover the Self.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and bahuvrīhi)
samasa.vigraha: चत्वारि अङ्गानि यस्य तत् चतुरङ्गम्; चतुरङ्गम् बलम् चतुरङ्गबलम्; चतुरङ्गबलस्य ईश्वरी चतुरङ्गबलेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: catvāri aṅgāni yasya tat caturaṅgam; caturaṅgam balam caturaṅgabalam; caturaṅgabalasya īśvarī caturaṅgabaleśvarī
samasa.explanation: (1) catur-aṅga 'having four limbs' (bahuvrīhi): the army's four arms — elephants, chariots, cavalry and infantry. (2) caturaṅga-bala 'the fourfold army' (karmadhāraya). (3) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head: 'sovereign of the fourfold army'. catur's final r simply joins aṅga.

names.meaning: She who is sovereign of the fourfold army
names.significance: The classical Indian army had four arms; in the Lalitopākhyāna Her own hosts — elephant, horse and chariot corps and foot-soldiers — fight under Her command.

meaning_check.note: 'armies of four types' made exact: one army of four divisions, of which She is the sovereign.

names.previous_split_issues: baleśvarī was left as one row; it is bala 'army' + īśvarī 'sovereign', joined by guṇa.

samasa.explanation: As in name 685: dāyinī 'giving' (agent noun in -in from √dā) is the head and sāmrājya 'empire' its object.

components.note: abstract noun from samrāj 'universal sovereign' (sam + √rāj; the m of sam stays before rāj, Pāṇini 8.3.25 mo rāji samaḥ kvau)

names.meaning: She who is the bestower of imperial dominion
names.significance: Beyond a kingdom (685) She grants empire; traditionally the highest empire is liberation, sovereignty over all.

samasa.explanation: satya 'true' qualifies sandhā 'promise, compact', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose promise is true'. The feminine satyā takes its masculine stem satya inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva).

names.meaning: She who is true to Her word
names.significance: Her promise of protection to those who take refuge in Her never fails.

meaning_check.note: sandhā is a promise or vow; 'devoted to truth' is the loose sense, 'whose promise is true' the exact one.

samasa.explanation: mekhalā 'girdle' is identified with sāgara 'the ocean(s)', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose girdle is the ocean'.

names.meaning: She who is girdled by the oceans
names.significance: 'Ocean-girdled' is a classical epithet of the Earth; She is the Earth, with the encircling seas as Her waistband.

components.note: √dīkṣ 'to consecrate oneself (for a rite)', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is consecrated (dīkṣitā)
names.significance: Traditionally read both ways: She is the consecrated sacrificer of the cosmic rite, and She is the one in whom initiation (dīkṣā) resides and who gives it to the devotee, removing bondage.

meaning_check.note: 'under a vow' narrowed the word; dīkṣita is one consecrated for a rite. The active reading ('who initiates') is given in the significance.

names.uncertain: The participle is passive ('consecrated'), but the name is commonly explained as 'She who initiates', taking dīkṣitā as 'possessed of dīkṣā'; both are current.

samasa.explanation: śamanī 'one who quells' is an agent noun in -ana from the causative of √śam 'to be calm', feminine; daitya 'demon' stands to it as the object, in the genitive.

components.note: vṛddhi derivative of Diti, the demons' mother

names.meaning: She who subdues the demons
names.significance: Outwardly She destroys the demon hosts of the Purāṇas; inwardly She quells the demonic tendencies in the heart.

meaning_check.note: 'wicked forces' moved to the significance; śamanī is 'one who quells, subdues'.

sandhi.rule: the m (an augment inserted after the object, as in priyaṅkara) becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ) and then the nasal of the following k's class, ṅ (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे लोकाः सर्वलोकाः; सर्वलोकान् वशम् करोति इति सर्वलोकवशङ्करी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve lokāḥ sarvalokāḥ; sarvalokān vaśam karoti iti sarvalokavaśaṅkarī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-loka 'all the worlds' (karmadhāraya). (2) vaśaṅ-karī 'one who brings under control' (vaśa 'control' + kara from √kṛ, with the augment m after vaśa and the feminine -ī). (3) The worlds are the object of that action: 'She who brings all the worlds under Her sway'.

names.meaning: She who keeps all the worlds under Her control
names.significance: All beings move by Her will; in worship She is invoked to draw all to Her (vaśīkaraṇa), and the true subjugation is of one's own mind.
names.previous_split_issues: vaśaṅkarī was left as one row; it is vaśa 'control' + karī 'making', with the augment m (written ṅ before k).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे अर्थाः सर्वार्थाः; सर्वार्थानाम् दात्री सर्वार्थदात्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve arthāḥ sarvārthāḥ; sarvārthānām dātrī sarvārthadātrī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-artha 'all aims, all things sought' (karmadhāraya). (2) dātrī 'giver' (agent noun in -tṛ from √dā, feminine) is the head and takes them as its object in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who grants all desires
names.significance: Artha is all that is sought; traditionally the name covers all four aims of life — dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa.
names.previous_split_issues: sarvārtha was left as one row; it is sarva + artha, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

components.meaning: belonging to Savitṛ, the Sun as Impeller; the Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī) verse
components.note: vṛddhi derivative of savitṛ, from √sū 'to impel, bring forth', feminine

names.meaning: She who is Sāvitrī, the impelling power of the Sun that brings the worlds forth
names.significance: Sāvitrī is the Ṛgvedic verse to Savitṛ (the Gāyatrī) and its goddess; from the root √sū 'to bring forth' the name is read as the creative power that impels the universe.

meaning_check.note: The name Sāvitrī and its link to Savitṛ are now stated; the creative sense is kept.

sandhi.rule: ścutva: t becomes c before c (Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ)
jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) (over an inner samāhāra-dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: सत् च चित् च आनन्दः च सच्चिदानन्दम्; सच्चिदानन्दम् एव रूपम् सच्चिदानन्दरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sat ca cit ca ānandaḥ ca saccidānandam; saccidānandam eva rūpam saccidānandarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti saccidānandarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) sat-cit-ānanda 'being, consciousness and bliss' taken together as one whole (samāhāra-dvandva). (2) That whole is identified with rūpa 'form, nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in makes 'She whose form is being-consciousness-bliss'.

components.meaning: having the form, whose nature is

names.meaning: She who is of the nature of existence, consciousness and bliss
names.significance: Saccidānanda is the Vedāntic description of Brahman — not three qualities but one reality seen three ways — and She is that reality.
names.previous_split_issues: saccidānanda was left as one row; it is sat + cit + ānanda, joined by ścutva and jaśtva.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
a short vowel before ch takes the augment t (Pāṇini 6.1.73 che ca), which becomes c by ścutva (8.4.40): pari + chinnā → paricchinnā

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: देशः च कालः च देशकालौ; न परिच्छिन्ना अपरिच्छिन्ना; देशकालाभ्याम् अपरिच्छिन्ना देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना
samasa.vigraha_iast: deśaḥ ca kālaḥ ca deśakālau; na paricchinnā aparicchinnā; deśakālābhyām aparicchinnā deśakālāparicchinnā
samasa.explanation: (1) deśa-kāla 'space and time' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) a-paricchinnā 'not limited, not cut off' (nañ-tatpuruṣa on the participle of pari + √chid). (3) The pair stands in the instrumental of agent: 'not limited by space and time'.

components.note: a- 'not' + pari + √chid 'to cut', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is not limited by space and time
names.significance: Whatever is in space and time is bounded; She, the ground of space and time, is bounded by neither — present everywhere and at every moment.

meaning_check.note: The two near-identical glosses were merged into one.

names.previous_split_issues: kālāparicchinnā was left as one row; it is kāla + a-paricchinnā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.explanation: -ga 'going' from √gam (suffix ḍa after sarva and similar words, Pāṇini 3.2.48 antātyantādhvadūrapārasarvānanteṣu ḍaḥ), feminine -gā; sarva is its object: 'going to all, reaching everything'.

names.meaning: She who is all-pervading, present everywhere
names.significance: She pervades every world and every being, moving and unmoving, as the one consciousness in all.

meaning_check.note: The two glosses were merged; 'all-pervading' is the sense of sarvagā ('going to all').

samasa.explanation: mohinī 'deluding, enchanting' is an agent noun in -in from the causative of √muh 'to be bewildered', feminine; it governs sarva 'all' as its object.

names.meaning: She who deludes all
names.significance: By Her Māyā even the wise are bewildered; the same power that binds is withdrawn by Her grace.

components.meaning: Sarasvatī, goddess of learning and speech; 'she who has pools (of water)'
components.note: saras 'pool, lake' + the possessive suffix -vat, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge and speech
names.significance: Sarasvatī is the river-goddess of the Ṛgveda who became the goddess of speech and learning; She is that flowing knowledge.

meaning_check.note: The name Sarasvatī is now given; 'in the form of knowledge' is kept as its sense.

components.meaning: consisting of the scriptures, made of śāstra
components.note: śāstra 'teaching, scripture' + the suffix -maya 'consisting of', feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who consists of the scriptures
names.significance: The scriptures are Her form; traditionally the sciences and sacred texts are described as Her limbs.

meaning_check.note: The two glosses merged; 'whose limbs are the scriptures' is a traditional elaboration and moved to the significance.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the same surface results from guhā + ambā (ā + a → ā), which gives the second reading

samasa.vigraha: गुहस्य अम्बा गुहाम्बा; अथवा गुहायाम् अम्बा गुहाम्बा
samasa.vigraha_iast: guhasya ambā guhāmbā; athavā guhāyām ambā guhāmbā
samasa.explanation: ambā 'mother' is the head. With guha 'Skanda' in the genitive: 'the mother of Guha'. With guhā 'cave' in the locative: 'the mother in the cave (of the heart)'. The fused long ā hides whether the first member is guha or guhā.

names.meaning: She who is the mother of Guha (Skanda)
names.significance: As Pārvatī She is the mother of Skanda; read as guhā, She is the Mother hidden in the cave of the heart, where the Upaniṣads place the Self.

meaning_check.note: The two glosses are given as the two analyses of one compound; the meaning follows the first.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; guhāmbā is guha (or guhā) + ambā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.
names.uncertain: The fused ā allows guha 'Skanda' or guhā 'cave'; both readings are traditional.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau)
samasa.vigraha: गुह्यम् रूपम् गुह्यरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गुह्यरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: guhyam rūpam guhyarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti guhyarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) guhya 'secret' qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive suffix -in makes 'She who has a secret form'.

names.meaning: She who has a secret form
names.significance: Her true form is hidden from the senses and revealed only in the teacher's instruction and within; Her mantra and its inner sense are kept secret in Śrīvidyā.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
the final s of nis becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे उपाधयः सर्वोपाधयः; सर्वोपाधिभ्यः विनिर्मुक्ता सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve upādhayaḥ sarvopādhayaḥ; sarvopādhibhyaḥ vinirmuktā sarvopādhivinirmuktā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-upādhi 'all limiting adjuncts' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly released' is the head and takes them in the ablative: 'released from all limiting adjuncts'.

components.meaning: limiting adjunct, a condition that seems to limit the limitless

components.note: vi + nis + √muc 'to release', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is free of all limiting adjuncts (upādhi)
names.significance: In Vedānta body, mind and name are upādhis that seem to limit pure consciousness; She, as that consciousness, is untouched by all of them.

meaning_check.note: 'limitations' made exact: upādhi is a limiting adjunct.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvopādhi was left as one row; it is sarva + upādhi, joined by guṇa.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: सदा शिवः सदाशिवः; पतिः व्रतम् यस्याः सा पतिव्रता; सदाशिवस्य पतिव्रता सदाशिवपतिव्रता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadā śivaḥ sadāśivaḥ; patiḥ vratam yasyāḥ sā pativratā; sadāśivasya pativratā sadāśivapativratā
samasa.explanation: (1) sadā-śiva 'ever auspicious', the name of the fifth Brahma. (2) pati-vratā 'she whose vow is her husband', the faithful wife (bahuvrīhi). (3) Sadāśiva stands to her in the genitive: 'the faithful wife of Sadāśiva'.

components.note: vrata 'vow', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is the devoted wife of Sadāśiva
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā Sadāśiva is the highest of the five Brahmas, the Lord who grants grace; She is inseparable from Him as His faithful consort and power.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written Sadāśiva in IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: sadā was glossed 'true/good'; it is the adverb 'always' (Sadāśiva 'the Ever-Auspicious'). pativratā was left as one row (pati + vratā).

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head; sampradāya 'tradition handed down' stands to it in the genitive.

components.meaning: tradition handed down from teacher to disciple
components.note: sam + pra + √dā 'to give': what is fully handed over

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of the sacred traditions
names.significance: Sampradāya is teaching passed from teacher to disciple without a break; She presides over it and is its source, so knowledge received in the lineage is received from Her.

meaning_check.note: īśvarī is 'sovereign'; 'guardian' was looser.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; sampradāyeśvarī is sampradāya + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci). The surface sādhvī is read by Bhāskararāya as two names, 711 sādhu and 712 ī, because sādhvī as one word would repeat name 128; the junction between them is this sandhi.

components.note: √sādh 'to accomplish' + the Uṇādi suffix -u; used here as a name of the Goddess

names.meaning: She who is sādhu, the good and upright
names.significance: Bhāskararāya divides the surface sādhvī into two names so that name 128 (sādhvī) is not repeated: 711 sādhu 'the good' and 712 ī. She is goodness itself, straight and even toward all.

meaning_check.note: 'possesses equanimity' is an interpretation; the word means good, upright, even. The sense of evenness is kept in the meaning.

names.uncertain: Bhāskararāya's own gloss of sādhu could not be checked against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara; 'equanimity' (the earlier meaning) may reflect it.
names.variants: Lists that do not follow Bhāskararāya read sādhvī here as one name, repeating name 128.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci). The surface sādhvī is read by Bhāskararāya as two names, 711 sādhu and 712 ī, because sādhvī as one word would repeat name 128; the junction between them is this sandhi.

components.meaning: the long vowel ī; in Śrīvidyā the syllable of kāmakalā

names.meaning: She who is the syllable ī (kāmakalā)
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the long vowel ī is the letter of kāmakalā, the union of Śiva and Śakti that is the seed of creation (compare name 322, kāmakalārūpā); it stands in Her Pañcadaśī mantra.

meaning_check.note: The old meaning ('the symbol I') mixed in an editorial remark; the name is the vowel ī, and the note on other versions moved to variants.

names.uncertain: The kāmakalā reading is the Śrīvidyā one; single-syllable lexicons also give ī as a name of Lakṣmī. Bhāskararāya's exact gloss could not be checked against a printed text.
names.variants: Lists that do not follow Bhāskararāya read sādhvī (711–712) as one name, repeating name 128, and reach 1,000 by dividing elsewhere.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: गुरूणाम् मण्डलम् गुरुमण्डलम्; गुरुमण्डलम् एव रूपम् गुरुमण्डलरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: gurūṇām maṇḍalam gurumaṇḍalam; gurumaṇḍalam eva rūpam gurumaṇḍalarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti gurumaṇḍalarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) guru-maṇḍala 'the circle of gurus' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) That circle is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is the circle of gurus'.

names.meaning: She whose form is the circle (lineage) of the gurus
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā worship the lineage of teachers — the divine, the perfected and the human streams (divyaugha, siddhaugha, mānavaugha) — is worshipped as Her own form.

meaning_check.note: Rephrased to follow the compound: the guru-maṇḍala is Her form.

names.previous_split_issues: guru was given as gurū (long ū); the word is guru, as the corrected text reads.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
the d of ud becomes voiceless t before t (cartva, Pāṇini 8.4.55 khari ca)

samasa.explanation: The participle uttīrṇā 'having crossed over' is the head; kula stands to it as the thing crossed, in the accusative: 'She who has crossed beyond the kula'.

components.meaning: kula: the group (of the senses); family; the Kaula path; the region of the lower cakras

names.meaning: She who transcends the kula (the senses)
names.significance: Kula is a word of many senses in Śrīvidyā; taken as the group of the senses, She is beyond their reach. Taken as the Kaula path, She is also beyond every particular path of worship.

meaning_check.note: 'senses' is the commentarial sense of kula; the word itself is now named.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; kulottīrṇā is kula + uttīrṇā (ud + tīrṇā), joined by guṇa.
names.uncertain: kula has several traditional senses here — the senses, the Kaula path, the family of the knower–knowing–known; the reading as 'the senses' follows the earlier meaning.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; bhaga stands to it in the locative, as the place of worship: 'to be worshipped in the bhaga'.

components.meaning: the orb of the sun; also the downward triangle (trikoṇa); excellence, fortune

names.meaning: She who is worshipped in the sun's disc
names.significance: Bhaga is also a name of the Sun (one of the Ādityas), and She is meditated on within the solar orb; in Śrīcakra worship bhaga is also the central triangle, Her seat.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; bhagārādhyā is bhaga + ārādhyā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.
names.uncertain: bhaga can be taken as the sun's disc or as the trikoṇa of Śrīcakra; the meaning follows the first.

components.meaning: Māyā, the power that veils reality and projects the world; illusion

names.meaning: She who is Māyā, the power of illusion
names.significance: 'Know Prakṛti to be Māyā, and the great Lord the wielder of Māyā' (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.10). Her Māyā veils and projects the world, and by Her grace it is removed.

meaning_check.note: Named Māyā as a power, not a mere 'illusion'.

components.note: madhu 'honey, sweetness' + the possessive suffix -mat, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is full of sweetness
names.significance: Her nature is sweet as honey to the devotee; madhumatī is also the name of an advanced stage of yoga in the commentary on the Yoga Sūtras, and is traditionally read here too.

meaning_check.note: madhumatī is 'possessed of honey, full of sweetness'; 'whose nature is' was added.

names.previous_split_issues: matī was glossed 'full of/minded'; it is the possessive suffix -mat (feminine -matī), not a separate word, so the name is a derivative, not a compound.

names.meaning: She who is the Earth
names.significance: She is the great Earth that bears and nourishes all beings, as in name 694.

meaning_check.note: 'goddess earth' tidied; Mahī is a name of the Earth.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: ambā 'mother' is the head; gaṇa 'the troops (of Śiva)' stands to it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the mother of the Gaṇas, Śiva's attendants
names.significance: As Pārvatī She is mother to Śiva's hosts and to Gaṇeśa, their lord.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization and the word Gaṇa supplied.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; gaṇāmbā is gaṇa + ambā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a vowel or voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

verse_notes.note: The r in -mūrtir- is the visarga of aṣṭamūrtiḥ (662); name 663 begins ajā-, not rajā-.
Names 673–676 play on one root (√bṛh, whence brahman): bṛhatī, brāhmaṇī, brāhmī, brahmānandā.
The second half holds three names, not five: 681, 682 and 683 śobhanā sulabhā gatiḥ, which Bhāskararāya counts as one name (śobhanā alone would repeat name 462).
Names 684–692 are a run of royal names (rāja-, rājya-, sāmrājya-).
rājyalakṣmīḥ (689) keeps its visarga before kośanāthā: lakṣmī is not a derived feminine in -ī and takes -ḥ in the nominative (compare 210).
In deśakālāparicchinnā (701) the negative a- of aparicchinnā is hidden in the long ā of kālā-: the name says 'not limited' by space and time.

external_sandhi.rule: yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

verse_notes.note: साध्वी is two names in Bhāskararāya's division: 711 sādhu and 712 ī, since sādhvī is already name 128.
bhagārādhyā (715) and guhyakārādhyā (720) both end in ārādhyā 'to be worshipped', its ā fused with the preceding a.
Names 725–726 belong together: Dakṣiṇāmūrti and His disciples, Sanaka and the other sages.

report.summary: Checked all 66 names of ślokas 131–140 against text.json: sandhi at every member and prefix junction, layered samāsa analyses with pausa-form vigrahas, and each meaning against its analysis. Bhāskararāya's division of sādhvī into 711 sādhu + 712 ī (to avoid repeating name 128) and his single name 683 śobhanā sulabhā gatiḥ (avoiding a repeat of 462) are explained; meanings that misread a word were replaced (666 bhūman, 674, 686 vallabha, 687 rājat, 689 rājya, 712, and 723, which carried 708's meaning). No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
